claim: Detergents and lipid nanodiscs affect the cryo-EM structures of pentameric ligand-gated ion channels (pLGICs) including ELIC.
source: Detergents and lipid nanodiscs affect the cryo-EM structures of pentameric ligand-gated ion channels (pLGICs) including ELIC.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work and is presented as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: ELIC activation and desensitization were confirmed in liposomes with a stopped-flow thallium flux assay.
source: ELIC activation and desensitization were confirmed in liposomes with a stopped-flow thallium flux assay.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the stopped-flow thallium flux assay shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Using WT ELIC and a non-desensitizing mutant (ELIC5), resting, activated, and desensitized structures were captured at high resolution.
source: Using WT ELIC and a non-desensitizing mutant (ELIC5), we captured resting, activated, and desensitized structures at high resolution.
evidence: This claim is supported by the cryo-EM structures presented in Figure 2A and the resolution data in Supplementary file 1.

claim: In the desensitized structure, the ion conduction pore has a constriction at the 9' leucine of the pore-lining M2 helix.
source: In the desensitized structure, the ion conduction pore has a constriction at the 9' leucine of the pore-lining M2 helix, indicating that 9' is the desensitization gate in ELIC.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The 9' position is the desensitization gate in ELIC.
source: In the desensitized structure, the ion conduction pore has a constriction at the 9' leucine of the pore-lining M2 helix, indicating that 9' is the desensitization gate in ELIC.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the structural observation of the constriction at 9' in the desensitized state.

claim: The agonist-bound structures of ELIC in liposomes are distinct from those in nanodiscs.
source: The agonist-bound structures of ELIC in liposomes are distinct from those in nanodiscs.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparisons shown in Figure 4.

claim: The transmembrane domain is more loosely packed in liposomes compared to nanodiscs.
source: In general, the transmembrane domain is more loosely packed in liposomes compared to nanodiscs.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis data presented in Supplementary file 3.

claim: ELIC localizes to the rim of large circularized nanodiscs.
source: However, ELIC localizes to the rim of large circularized nanodiscs, and structures of ELIC in large nanodiscs deviate from the liposome structures more than those in small nanodiscs.
evidence: This claim is supported by cryo-EM micrographs and 2D class averages shown in Figure 3A and 3B.

claim: Structures of ELIC in large nanodiscs deviate from the liposome structures more than those in small nanodiscs.
source: However, ELIC localizes to the rim of large circularized nanodiscs, and structures of ELIC in large nanodiscs deviate from the liposome structures more than those in small nanodiscs.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparisons shown in Figure 4.

claim: In the α1 glycine receptor (GlyR), the proportion of particles contributing to open and desensitized conformations differed when using detergent, MSP (membrane scaffold protein) nanodiscs, or SMA (styrene maleic acid) extracted nanoparticles.
source: In the α1 glycine receptor (GlyR), the proportion of particles contributing to open and desensitized conformations differed when using detergent, MSP (membrane scaffold protein) nanodiscs, or SMA (styrene maleic acid) extracted nanoparticles (Yu et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Yu et al., 2021.

claim: Different structures were obtained in detergent or various nanodiscs for the GABAA receptor (GABAAR).
source: In other pLGICs, different structures were obtained in detergent or various nanodiscs for the GABAA receptor (GABAAR) (Zhu et al., 2018; Kim et al., 2020), serotonin 3A receptor (5-HT3aR) (Basak et al., 2018a; Basak et al., 2018b; Zhang et al., 2021a), α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (α7 nAChR) (Noviello et al., 2021; Burke et al., 2024; Zhao et al., 2021), and muscle nAChR (Rahman et al., 2020; Zarkadas et al., 2022).

claim: Different structures were obtained in detergent or various nanodiscs for the serotonin 3A receptor (5-HT3aR).
source: In other pLGICs, different structures were obtained in detergent or various nanodiscs for the GABAA receptor (GABAAR) (Zhu et al., 2018; Kim et al., 2020), serotonin 3A receptor (5-HT3aR) (Basak et al., 2018a; Basak et al., 2018b; Zhang et al., 2021a), α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (α7 nAChR) (Noviello et al., 2021; Burke et al., 2024; Zhao et al., 2021), and muscle nAChR (Rahman et al., 2020; Zarkadas et al., 2022).

claim: Different structures were obtained in detergent or various nanodiscs for the α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (α7 nAChR).
source: In other pLGICs, different structures were obtained in detergent or various nanodiscs for the GABAA receptor (GABAAR) (Zhu et al., 2018; Kim et al., 2020), serotonin 3A receptor (5-HT3aR) (Basak et al., 2018a; Basak et al., 2018b; Zhang et al., 2021a), α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (α7 nAChR) (Noviello et al., 2021; Burke et al., 2024; Zhao et al., 2021), and muscle nAChR (Rahman et al., 2020; Zarkadas et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Noviello et al., 2021; Burke et al., 2024; Zhao et al., 2021.

claim: Different structures were obtained in detergent or various nanodiscs for muscle nAChR.
source: In other pLGICs, different structures were obtained in detergent or various nanodiscs for the GABAA receptor (GABAAR) (Zhu et al., 2018; Kim et al., 2020), serotonin 3A receptor (5-HT3aR) (Basak et al., 2018a; Basak et al., 2018b; Zhang et al., 2021a), α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (α7 nAChR) (Noviello et al., 2021; Burke et al., 2024; Zhao et al., 2021), and muscle nAChR (Rahman et al., 2020; Zarkadas et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Rahman et al., 2020; Zarkadas et al., 2022.

claim: In a systematic study of the prokaryotic pLGIC, ELIC, in which various lipid nanoparticles or nanodiscs were tested, it was shown that the choice of nanodisc affects the agonist-bound structure of ELIC.
source: In a systematic study of the prokaryotic pLGIC, ELIC, in which various lipid nanoparticles or nanodiscs were tested, it was shown that the choice of nanodisc affects the agonist-bound structure of ELIC (Dalal et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Dalal et al., 2024.

claim: Detergent or nanodisc conditions impact the structure of pLGICs.
source: Taken together, these studies indicate that detergent or nanodisc conditions impact the structure of pLGICs.
evidence: This claim is inferred from multiple cited studies showing structural variations in different membrane mimetics.

claim: Molecular dynamics simulations of ELIC in small nanodiscs show frequent contact of the scaffold with the membrane-facing M4 helix, altering the conformation and dynamics of this helix.
source: This is because molecular dynamics simulations of ELIC in small nanodiscs show frequent contact of the scaffold with the membrane-facing M4 helix, altering the conformation and dynamics of this helix (Dalal et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Dalal et al., 2024.

claim: The MSP perturbs the structure of the lipid bilayer (i.e. thickness and order) at the rim.
source: The MSP also perturbs the structure of the lipid bilayer (i.e. thickness and order) at the rim (Bengtsen et al., 2020), and this too may be undesirable.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Bengtsen et al., 2020.

claim: The function of the ABC transporter was found to be sensitive to nanodisc size with larger nanodiscs yielding functional properties that are more similar to the ABC transporter in liposomes.
source: In support of this notion, the function of the ABC transporter was found to be sensitive to nanodisc size with larger nanodiscs yielding functional properties that are more similar to the ABC transporter in liposomes (Nouel Barreto et al., 2025).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Nouel Barreto et al., 2025.

claim: Optimal reconstitution of ELIC in liposomes to facilitate single particle cryo-EM was achieved by dialysis.
source: Optimal reconstitution of ELIC in liposomes to facilitate single particle cryo-EM was achieved by dialysis.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental methods described in the manuscript.

claim: Reconstitution of ELIC in liposomes at low protein:lipid molar ratios can be accomplished by detergent removal with Biobeads.
source: Reconstitution of ELIC in liposomes at low protein:lipid molar ratios can be accomplished by detergent removal with Biobeads (Petroff et al., 2022); however, reconstitution at a higher protein:lipid molar ratio (1:500 in this study) with efficient incorporation of ELIC in the liposomes required dialysis.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Petroff et al., 2022 and experimental data from this study.

claim: Reconstitution at a higher protein:lipid molar ratio (1:500 in this study) with efficient incorporation of ELIC in the liposomes required dialysis.
source: Reconstitution of ELIC in liposomes at low protein:lipid molar ratios can be accomplished by detergent removal with Biobeads (Petroff et al., 2022); however, reconstitution at a higher protein:lipid molar ratio (1:500 in this study) with efficient incorporation of ELIC in the liposomes required dialysis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from this study.

claim: The method was adapted from protocols previously reported for the reconstitution of muscle nAChR, 5-HT3aR, and ELIC.
source: The method was adapted from protocols previously reported for the reconstitution of muscle nAChR (daCosta et al., 2009), 5-HT3aR (Kudryashev et al., 2016), and ELIC (Carswell et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to daCosta et al., 2009; Kudryashev et al., 2016; Carswell et al., 2015.

claim: Proteoliposomes were formed using a 2:1:1 molar ratio of POPC:POPE:POPG.
source: Proteoliposomes were formed using a 2:1:1 molar ratio of POPC (1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-phosphatidylcholine):POPE (1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-phosphatidylethanolamine):POPG (1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-phosphatidylglycerol); these lipids are known to support ELIC activity (Petroff et al., 2022), and phosphatidylethanolamine and phosphatidylglycerol are the two principal phospholipids found in gram-negative bacteria in which ELIC is expressed.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from this study.

claim: POPC:POPE:POPG lipids are known to support ELIC activity.
source: Proteoliposomes were formed using a 2:1:1 molar ratio of POPC (1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-phosphatidylcholine):POPE (1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-phosphatidylethanolamine):POPG (1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-phosphatidylglycerol); these lipids are known to support ELIC activity (Petroff et al., 2022), and phosphatidylethanolamine and phosphatidylglycerol are the two principal phospholipids found in gram-negative bacteria in which ELIC is expressed.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Petroff et al., 2022.

claim: Phosphatidylethanolamine and phosphatidylglycerol are the two principal phospholipids found in gram-negative bacteria in which ELIC is expressed.
source: Proteoliposomes were formed using a 2:1:1 molar ratio of POPC (1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-phosphatidylcholine):POPE (1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-phosphatidylethanolamine):POPG (1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-phosphatidylglycerol); these lipids are known to support ELIC activity (Petroff et al., 2022), and phosphatidylethanolamine and phosphatidylglycerol are the two principal phospholipids found in gram-negative bacteria in which ELIC is expressed.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about bacterial membrane composition.

claim: WT ELIC activates and then mostly desensitizes in response to the agonist, propylamine.
source: Using a stopped-flow thallium flux assay, we confirmed that WT ELIC activates and then mostly desensitizes in response to the agonist, propylamine (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The time constant of activation and desensitization was 10 ± 2 ms and 5.1 ± 2.1 s (± SD, n = 6), respectively.
source: The time constant of activation and desensitization was 10 ± 2 ms and 5.1 ± 2.1 s (± SD, n = 6), respectively, which matches the kinetics of ELIC activation and desensitization from excised patch-clamp recordings in liposomes or HEK293 cells (Marabelli et al., 2015; Laha et al., 2013; Tong et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the stopped-flow thallium flux assay.

claim: The kinetics of ELIC activation and desensitization in liposomes matches those from excised patch-clamp recordings in liposomes or HEK293 cells.
source: The time constant of activation and desensitization was 10 ± 2 ms and 5.1 ± 2.1 s (± SD, n = 6), respectively, which matches the kinetics of ELIC activation and desensitization from excised patch-clamp recordings in liposomes or HEK293 cells (Marabelli et al., 2015; Laha et al., 2013; Tong et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison with data from cited studies.

claim: ELIC5 (P254G/C300S/V261Y/G319F/I320F) eliminates channel desensitization.
source: We previously identified a combination of five mutations in ELIC, P254G/C300S/V261Y/G319F/I320F, called ELIC5 which eliminates channel desensitization (Petroff et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Petroff et al., 2022.

claim: ELIC5 in 2:1:1 POPC:POPE:POPG liposomes activates and does not desensitize for at least 20 min.
source: We confirmed that ELIC5 in 2:1:1 POPC:POPE:POPG liposomes activates and does not desensitize for at least 20 min (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The open probability of ELIC5 when activated by 10 mM propylamine in 2:1:1 POPC:POPE:POPG membranes is estimated to be close to 1.
source: The open probability of ELIC5 when activated by 10 mM propylamine in 2:1:1 POPC:POPE:POPG membranes is estimated to be close to 1 (Petroff et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Petroff et al., 2022.

claim: Proteoliposome preparations of WT ELIC in the absence and presence of propylamine are expected to yield resting and desensitized channels, respectively.
source: Therefore, proteoliposome preparations of WT ELIC in the absence and presence of propylamine are expected to yield resting and desensitized channels, respectively, and ELIC5 in the presence of propylamine is expected to yield activated channels.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the functional characterization data.

claim: ELIC5 in the presence of propylamine is expected to yield activated channels.
source: Therefore, proteoliposome preparations of WT ELIC in the absence and presence of propylamine are expected to yield resting and desensitized channels, respectively, and ELIC5 in the presence of propylamine is expected to yield activated channels.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the functional characterization data.

claim: Side views from the 2D class averages showed that ELIC is oriented in both directions in the liposomes with a preference for the extracellular domain (ECD) facing the extra-liposomal solution (i.e. outward-facing orientation).
source: Side views from the 2D class averages showed that ELIC is oriented in both directions in the liposomes with a preference for the extracellular domain (ECD) facing the extra-liposomal solution (i.e. outward-facing orientation) (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by 2D class averages shown in the figures.

claim: Heterogeneous refinement in CryoSPARC separated the particles into two classes that generated outward- and inward-facing 3D reconstructions.
source: Heterogeneous refinement in CryoSPARC separated the particles into two classes that generated outward- and inward-facing 3D reconstructions (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the 3D reconstructions shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Final maps were obtained for apo WT ELIC at a resolution of 3.4 Å for outward-facing and 3.6 Å for inward-facing channels.
source: Nevertheless, final maps were obtained for apo WT ELIC at a resolution of 3.4 Å for outward-facing and 3.6 Å for inward-facing channels, agonist-bound WT ELIC at a resolution of 3.8 Å for outward-facing and 4.2 Å for inward-facing channels, and agonist-bound ELIC5 at a resolution of 2.8 Å for outward-facing and 4.2 Å for inward-facing channels (Figure 2A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Figure 1—figure supplement 3, Figure 1—figure supplement 4, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the cryo-EM maps and resolution data.

claim: Final maps were obtained for agonist-bound WT ELIC at a resolution of 3.8 Å for outward-facing and 4.2 Å for inward-facing channels.
source: Nevertheless, final maps were obtained for apo WT ELIC at a resolution of 3.4 Å for outward-facing and 3.6 Å for inward-facing channels, agonist-bound WT ELIC at a resolution of 3.8 Å for outward-facing and 4.2 Å for inward-facing channels, and agonist-bound ELIC5 at a resolution of 2.8 Å for outward-facing and 4.2 Å for inward-facing channels (Figure 2A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Figure 1—figure supplement 3, Figure 1—figure supplement 4, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the cryo-EM maps and resolution data.

claim: Final maps were obtained for agonist-bound ELIC5 at a resolution of 2.8 Å for outward-facing and 4.2 Å for inward-facing channels.
source: Nevertheless, final maps were obtained for apo WT ELIC at a resolution of 3.4 Å for outward-facing and 3.6 Å for inward-facing channels, agonist-bound WT ELIC at a resolution of 3.8 Å for outward-facing and 4.2 Å for inward-facing channels, and agonist-bound ELIC5 at a resolution of 2.8 Å for outward-facing and 4.2 Å for inward-facing channels (Figure 2A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Figure 1—figure supplement 3, Figure 1—figure supplement 4, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the cryo-EM maps and resolution data.

claim: In all samples, the inward- and outward-facing structures of ELIC were not significantly different.
source: In all samples, the inward- and outward-facing structures of ELIC were not significantly different.
evidence: This claim is based on structural comparison of the inward- and outward-facing maps.

claim: The inward-facing structures were of significantly lower resolution and quality compared to the outward-facing structures.
source: However, we cannot be certain that ELIC structure is insensitive to membrane curvature due to the limitations of distinguishing inward- and outward-facing particles. In addition, the inward-facing structures were of significantly lower resolution and quality compared to the outward-facing structures.
evidence: This claim is supported by the resolution data and quality of the cryo-EM maps.

claim: The structures of ELIC in liposomes have the same overall architecture as structures of ELIC or other pLGICs in nanodiscs, consisting of a homopentameric assembly around a central ion conduction pore.
source: The structures of ELIC in liposomes have the same overall architecture as structures of ELIC or other pLGICs in nanodiscs, consisting of a homopentameric assembly around a central ion conduction pore (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by the cryo-EM structures shown in Figure 2.

claim: Each subunit consists of an ECD and TMD.
source: Each subunit consists of an ECD and TMD.
evidence: This claim is supported by the structural data shown in Figure 2.

claim: In the agonist-bound structures, propylamine binds in a conserved site between β-sheets from two adjacent subunits.
source: In the agonist-bound structures, propylamine binds in a conserved site between β-sheets from two adjacent subunits.
evidence: This claim is supported by the structural data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: ELIC activation consists of a contraction of the agonist binding site, counter-clockwise twisting of the ECD, and outward translation of M2–M3 linker and pre-M1 linker in the TMD.
source: ELIC activation consists of a contraction of the agonist binding site, counter-clockwise twisting of the ECD, and outward translation of M2–M3 linker and pre-M1 linker in the TMD (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: These changes are also associated with an outward translation and counter-clockwise twisting of the transmembrane helices (M1–M4) that leads to opening of the ion channel pore lined by the M2 helix.
source: These changes are also associated with an outward translation and counter-clockwise twisting of the transmembrane helices (M1–M4) that leads to opening of the ion channel pore lined by the M2 helix (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: ELIC desensitization consists of a partial return of the transmembrane helices (clockwise twisting and contraction), but without significant change in the ECD or the M2–M3 and pre-M1 linkers in the TMD.
source: ELIC desensitization consists of a partial return of the transmembrane helices (clockwise twisting and contraction), but without significant change in the ECD or the M2–M3 and pre-M1 linkers in the TMD (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Apo WT ELIC shows a pore with two hydrophobic constrictions at F247 and L240 (also known as 16' and 9' positions of M2), where the ion conduction pathway is dehydrated and therefore, closed.
source: Apo WT ELIC shows a pore with two hydrophobic constrictions at F247 and L240 (also known as 16' and 9' positions of M2), where the ion conduction pathway is dehydrated and therefore, closed (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: In agonist-bound ELIC5, the pore is hydrated and open because M2 rotates and F247 and L240 orient away from the pore axis toward the adjacent subunit.
source: In contrast, the agonist-bound ELIC5 pore is hydrated and open because M2 rotates and F247 and L240 orient away from the pore axis toward the adjacent subunit (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Agonist-bound WT ELIC shows conformational heterogeneity at F247, and two states were modeled with different conformations for F247 and Y248.
source: Agonist-bound WT ELIC shows conformational heterogeneity at F247, and two states were modeled with different conformations for F247 and Y248 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: In State 1, F247 orients toward the pore axis, while in State 2, F247 orients toward M2 of the adjacent subunit.
source: In State 1, F247 orients toward the pore axis, while in State 2, F247 orients toward M2 of the adjacent subunit.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: In State 2 of agonist-bound WT ELIC, 9' (L240) forms a hydrophobic constriction (diameter of 3.3 Å) like Apo WT ELIC (diameter of 2.6 Å).
source: The latter has a wider pore at 16' (F247), but still 9' (L240) forms a hydrophobic constriction (diameter of 3.3 Å) like Apo WT ELIC (diameter of 2.6 Å) (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The pore diameter at 9' (L240) and the hydrophobicity of this residue suggest that 9' is the highest barrier to ion conduction in the agonist-bound WT ELIC structure.
source: Nevertheless, the pore diameter at 9' (L240) and the hydrophobicity of this residue suggest that 9' is the highest barrier to ion conduction in the agonist-bound WT ELIC structure.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the structural data on pore dimensions and residue properties.

claim: Apo and agonist-bound WT ELIC are closed structures with hydrophobic constrictions at 9' consistent with resting and desensitized states.
source: In summary, apo and agonist-bound WT ELIC are closed structures with hydrophobic constrictions at 9' consistent with resting and desensitized states, and agonist-bound ELIC5 is an open structure consistent with an activated state.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the structural data on pore dimensions and functional characterization.

claim: Agonist-bound ELIC5 is an open structure consistent with an activated state.
source: In summary, apo and agonist-bound WT ELIC are closed structures with hydrophobic constrictions at 9' consistent with resting and desensitized states, and agonist-bound ELIC5 is an open structure consistent with an activated state.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the structural data on pore dimensions and functional characterization.

claim: It has been proposed that the activation and desensitization gates in the GABAAR and GlyR are distinct with 9' being the activation gate and –2' the desensitization gate.
source: It has been proposed that the activation and desensitization gates in the GABAAR and GlyR are distinct with 9' being the activation gate and –2' the desensitization gate (Yu et al., 2021; Masiulis et al., 2019; Kumar et al., 2020a; Gielen and Corringer, 2018; Gielen et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In agonist-bound structures of the α7 nAChR and 5-HT3aR, which are expected to be desensitized conformations, 9' is the only constriction in the pore that poses an energetic barrier to ion and water permeation.
source: However, in agonist-bound structures of the α7 nAChR and 5-HT3aR, which are expected to be desensitized conformations, 9' is the only constriction in the pore that poses an energetic barrier to ion and water permeation (Basak et al., 2018a; Noviello et al., 2021; Polovinkin et al., 2018; Zhuang et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: It was previously suggested that the agonist-bound structures of ELIC and 5-HT3aR may be pre-active states.
source: It was previously suggested that the agonist-bound structures of ELIC and 5-HT3aR may be pre-active states (Petroff et al., 2022; Felt et al., 2024), and that the channel may somehow be limited from entering a desensitized state due to detergent or nanodisc conditions (Dalal et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Petroff et al., 2022 and Felt et al., 2024.

claim: The channel may somehow be limited from entering a desensitized state due to detergent or nanodisc conditions.
source: It was previously suggested that the agonist-bound structures of ELIC and 5-HT3aR may be pre-active states (Petroff et al., 2022; Felt et al., 2024), and that the channel may somehow be limited from entering a desensitized state due to detergent or nanodisc conditions (Dalal et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Dalal et al., 2024.

claim: Based on the liposome structures, 9' is the desensitization gate for ELIC and possibly other cation-selective pLGICs.
source: Based on the liposome structures, we conclude that 9' is the desensitization gate for ELIC and possibly other cation-selective pLGICs.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the structural data in liposomes.

claim: Mutation of 9' (L240A) in ELIC appears to eliminate desensitization.
source: This conclusion is consistent with studies showing that mutation of 9' (L240A) in ELIC appears to eliminate desensitization (Gonzalez-Gutierrez et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Gonzalez-Gutierrez et al., 2012.

claim: Lipid-like densities are resolved in the agonist-bound ELIC5 structure.
source: Lipid-like densities are also resolved in the agonist-bound ELIC5 structure (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by the cryo-EM map shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The most prominent lipid densities are in the outer TMD consisting of four lipid-like tails.
source: The most prominent lipid densities are in the outer TMD consisting of four lipid-like tails.
evidence: This claim is supported by the cryo-EM map shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Two of these tails fill intersubunit (M1–M3) and intrasubunit (M3–M4) grooves and meet to form a putative phospholipid headgroup near R117 of the β6–β7 interfacial loops.
source: Two of these tails fill intersubunit (M1–M3) and intrasubunit (M3–M4) grooves and meet to form a putative phospholipid headgroup near R117 of the β6–β7 interfacial loops.
evidence: This claim is supported by the cryo-EM map shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: A very similar phospholipid density was observed previously in agonist-bound ELIC5 in nanodiscs (e.g. MSP1E3D1).
source: A very similar phospholipid density was observed previously in agonist-bound ELIC5 in nanodiscs (e.g. MSP1E3D1) (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), and streamlined free energy perturbation calculations determined that this is likely POPG and not POPE or POPC (Petroff et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison with prior structures and citation to Petroff et al., 2022.

claim: Streamlined free energy perturbation calculations determined that this is likely POPG and not POPE or POPC.
source: A very similar phospholipid density was observed previously in agonist-bound ELIC5 in nanodiscs (e.g. MSP1E3D1) (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), and streamlined free energy perturbation calculations determined that this is likely POPG and not POPE or POPC (Petroff et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Petroff et al., 2022.

claim: The lipid densities observed in the liposome structure of the activated state of ELIC are very similar to those observed in a nanodisc structure, suggesting that ELIC and not the nanodisc is primarily determining the interaction of these phospholipids.
source: Therefore, the lipid densities observed in the liposome structure of the activated state of ELIC are very similar to those observed in a nanodisc structure, suggesting that ELIC and not the nanodisc is primarily determining the interaction of these phospholipids.
evidence: This claim is inferred from comparison of lipid densities in liposome and nanodisc structures.

claim: Initial inspection of the micrographs showed multiple ELIC particles in most nanodiscs and localization of the particles to the rim of the nanodisc.
source: Initial inspection of the micrographs showed multiple ELIC particles in most nanodiscs and localization of the particles to the rim of the nanodisc (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by cryo-EM micrographs shown in Figure 3A.
